title: Grothendieck's existence theorem for closed subschemes of projective space over a complete Noetherian ring
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] complete with respect to an ideal $I$ [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], and let $X$ be a scheme over $A$ admitting, for some $n\ge0$, a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] $X\to\mathbf P^n_A$ over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ into projective space $\mathbf P^n_A=\operatorname{Spec}A\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. Put $\mathcal I=I\mathcal O_X$. Then the completion functor $\mathit{Coh}(\mathcal O_X)\to\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] is an equivalence of categories; in particular every object $(\mathcal F_n)$ of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ is isomorphic to $\mathcal F^\wedge$ for a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$ [pqf-def-coherent].

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0885 (lemma-existence-projective), Section 087V (section-existence), for X -> Spec(A) H-projective, which is projective by Morphisms Lemma 01W9 (lemma-H-projective); its proof uses Lemmas 0883, 0884 (lemma-vanishing-projective), 087Y (lemma-inverse-systems-surjective), 087X, 0881 (lemma-exact)

proof.text: The closed immersion into $\mathbf P^n_A$ makes $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ projective and supplies the $f$-ample invertible module $\mathcal L=i^*\mathcal O(1)$ [lem-weil-pbc-projective-ample-invertible]. The Noetherian and adic hypotheses therefore put $X$, $\mathcal I=I\mathcal O_X$, and the completion functor in the setting of [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module].

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0885 hypotheses and Morphisms Lemma 01W9 (lemma-H-projective)

proof.text: The completion functor is fully faithful for a proper morphism over a complete Noetherian ring by [lem-weil-pbc-formal-completion-fully-faithful-proper]. Since a projective morphism is proper, this applies to $f$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 0885, first paragraph, invoking Lemma 0883 (lemma-fully-faithful)

proof.text: For any formal coherent system $(\mathcal F_n)$, [lem-weil-pbc-vanishing-projective] gives an integer $d_0$ such that the first cohomology of every successive kernel $\operatorname{Ker}(\mathcal F_{n+1}\to\mathcal F_n)$, after tensoring with $\mathcal L^{\otimes d}$, vanishes for $d\ge d_0$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 0885, paragraph beginning 'Choose d_0 as in Lemma 0884'

proof.text: Choose $d\ge d_0$ so that $\mathcal F_1\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes d}$ is generated by finitely many global sections $s_{1,1},\ldots,s_{t,1}$; this is [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-twist-global-generation] applied to the coherent module $\mathcal F_1$ and the ample module $\mathcal L$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 0885, paragraph beginning 'Choose a d >= d_0' and Properties Proposition 01Q3

proof.text: The short exact sequences $0\to\operatorname{Ker}(\mathcal F_{n+1}\to\mathcal F_n)\to\mathcal F_{n+1}\to\mathcal F_n\to0$, after tensoring by $\mathcal L^{\otimes d}$, and the vanishing in Step 3 show that the transition maps $H^0(X,\mathcal F_{n+1}\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes d})\to H^0(X,\mathcal F_n\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes d})$ are surjective. Inductively lift each $s_{j,1}$ to a compatible system $s_{j,n}$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 0885, paragraph beginning 'Since the transition maps of the system'

proof.text: The compatible sections define a morphism of formal systems $((\mathcal L^{\otimes -d})^{\oplus t})^\wedge\to(\mathcal F_n)$. Its component at level $1$ is surjective by the choice of the $s_{j,1}$, hence the whole morphism is an epimorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-formal-systems-surjective]. Thus every coherent formal system is a quotient of an object in the image of completion.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 0885, paragraph beginning 'These determine a compatible system of maps' and Lemma 087Y

proof.text: Because $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ is abelian by [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-abelian], the kernel of the epimorphism in Step 6 is an object of the same category. Applying Step 6 to that kernel and composing its epimorphism with the kernel inclusion shows that every object is a cokernel of a morphism between two completed coherent modules.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 0885, paragraph beginning 'The result of the previous paragraph' and Lemma 087X

proof.text: The completion functor is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-formal-completion-exact] and fully faithful by Step 2. Therefore the cokernel of any morphism between completed coherent modules is itself the completion of the cokernel of the unique corresponding morphism of coherent modules. Step 7 then gives essential surjectivity, while Step 2 gives full faithfulness; hence the completion functor is an equivalence.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 0885, final paragraph invoking Lemmas 0883 and 0881
